readings.title: A form with fewer surprises
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Riverbank Service Desk watched volunteers try a new online application form. Many stopped at a page asking for a document they had not prepared. Designers added an opening checklist and allowed users to save progress before uploading files. Completion became easier, although some residents still preferred assistance at the desk. Staff kept that option and explained how saved information could be deleted. The improvement came from observing where people became stuck, rather than from adding a more attractive welcome image. A service was easier to use when its requirements became visible before the user had invested time.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: The helper who kept her hands back
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: During a digital-skills session, a volunteer could complete a visitor's task much faster by taking the mouse. She resisted that temptation and explained one step at a time while the visitor remained in control. When private information was needed, she turned away and reminded the visitor not to share passwords. The task took longer, but the visitor repeated several steps without help the following week. Assistance had supported both learning and privacy. The session was not successful merely because a form was submitted; it also mattered whether the person could understand and control what happened.

readings.title: Plain words on a public notice
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A council notice used the phrase 'commence the renewal procedure' beside a button. In a short session with residents, several people hesitated because they were unsure whether clicking would submit a final request. The wording was changed to 'Start renewing your permit', and the next steps were shown underneath. This did not make the legal conditions shorter or simpler than they really were. Those conditions remained available with an explanation. Clear language helped users know what an action would do. The team learnt that formal wording could create uncertainty without adding useful precision.

readings.title: The queue outside the website
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: When a booking service moved online, telephone calls initially fell. Managers took this as evidence that everyone found the website easy. At a community meeting, however, several residents said they had given up trying because they lacked internet access at home. Staff then compared completed bookings with calls and face-to-face requests. They introduced assisted booking hours and publicised the telephone option again. The original fall in calls had measured only one part of the experience. A quieter channel could indicate success, but it could also mean that some people had stopped reaching the service at all.

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

Moving a public service online can save time, but convenience is not the same for everyone. Some people need assistance with an unfamiliar form or device. A well-designed service offers clear language and another way to ask for help. Technology should widen access rather than create a new barrier.
translation.referenceAnswer: 把公共服务搬到网上可以节省时间，但并非每个人都能同样方便地使用。有些人在面对不熟悉的表格或设备时需要协助。设计良好的服务应提供清晰的语言以及其他求助方式。技术应扩大服务的可及性，而不是制造新的障碍。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Write a short article on making online public services easier to use. Consider people with limited digital experience and propose support.
writing.sampleAnswer: Online public services should be designed around the tasks people need to complete. Forms should use familiar words and list required documents before the first page, so users do not discover an unexpected requirement halfway through. Saving progress would help those who need to pause. People with limited digital experience should be able to obtain assistance by telephone or at a local service desk. A helper should guide the user without taking control of private accounts or asking for passwords. The service should also listen to people who fail to complete an application, not only to successful users. Easier digital access is valuable, but it works best when clear information and human support remain available together.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：观点、建议与应用文
